newsitem.title: UK: Latin America focus of new sugar freight business.
newsitem.headline: Latin America focus of new sugar freight business.

text.p: London's sugar freight market saw a spate of new orders on Monday, as Mexico and Costa Rica started to take over from Brazil as main western hemisphere suppliers before Cuban sugar comes properly on-stream, shipbrokers said.
Iran was also popular as an end-destination and featured in two new orders for bagged sugar, they said.
Iranian shippers IRISL quoted for 14,000 tonnes from Antwerp-Hamburg range for November/10 December and Seabon for 14,000 tonnes min/max from the EU for prompt/10 days.
Elsewhere, Costa Rica was reported to have sold 40,000 tonnes of raw sugar from its 1996/97 cane crop, with 15,000 tonnes to be shipped for February/March and 25,000 tonnes for March/May.
Details of the buyers and destinations of the sugar have yet to emerge.

Louis Dreyfus was in the market with two bagged orders, quoting for 8,100 tonnes from Coatzacoalcos to east coast South America for November dates and 3,850 tonnes from Le Havre to Praia and Mindelo for spot/prompt shipment.
Cargill was open with two bulk north Brazil orders for European destinations.

It quoted for 14,000 tonnes to the Black Sea with Egyptian Mediterranean option for 11/13 November and a further 16/25,000 tonnes from Maceio or Recife to Morocco, Black Sea, East Med and Baltic options for 15/25 November.
Cargill was also in the market for 3/3,300 tonnes of bagged sugar from Guayaquil to Haiti for prompt/November dates.
Ceba Shipping was open on account for a 14,000-tonne min/max bagged cargo from north Spain to Skaw range including the UK for November dates with 10 days notice.
Shyvers Savoy quoted an account order for 4,000 tonnes of bagged sugar, with possibility of raising to 5,000, from Dunkirk to Dakar and Nouakchott for 21/27 November.
It also quoted another order for 12,000 tonnes in bulk from Reunion to Nantes for 10/20 December.

Nouakchott also featured as a destination in two other bagged inquiries, as Madre Shipping quoted for 12,000 tonnes min/max from Veracruz to Douala-Nouakchott range for 20/25 November and Secretan for 6,000 tonnes from Antwerp for 14 November onwards.
Secretan issued a spate of other bagged orders, mainly from European and Brazilian origins.

Of the European origins, Secretan was open for 3/4,000 tonnes from Antwerp/Dunkirk to Algeria for prompt/14 days notice, 4,000 from Dunkirk to Batumi for 23/27 November and 2,000 from Visby to Klaipeda for 14/18 November.
It issued three north Brazilian orders -- 5,000 tonnes to Abidjan for 15/20 November, a further 5,000 to Dakar for 20/25 November and 7,500 from Maceio to Matadi for 18/22 November.
Secretan also quoted for 9/12,000 tonnes from Santos to Dar es Salaam plus other options for 22/27 November.
Allen Chartering quoted two account orders for bagged sugar, 12,000 tonnes from Veracruz to west coast Africa for 20/25 November and 6,000 from Madagascar to Mombasa for 9/13 November.
